content:
This module is a pre-completion checklist for error handling work: a short set of checks to run before calling a error handling task done.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When error handling decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
2. Measure before optimizing any error handling bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
3. Before starting error handling work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
4. Prefer the simplest error handling approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
5. Re-check edge cases relevant to error handling (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
6. Validate error handling outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
7. Document any non-obvious error handling decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
8. Keep error handling changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
9. Surface known limitations of a chosen error handling approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic error handling advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not silently drop error handling edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting error handling assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid introducing new error handling abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated error handling concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about error handling over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
